South Africa’s Second-Largest Bank FNB Launches Crypto Trading With VALR First National Bank (FNB), part of South Africa’s second-largest banking group by assets, has launched a crypto investing service allowing customers to trade BTC, ETH, XRP, SOL and USDT through its existing share-trading platform in partnership with licensed local exchange VALR. Trading is available 24/7 from as little as R10, with FNB saying the service responds to growing customer demand and that additional crypto investment options are planned. — link

Bitcoin ETFs Draw $119 Million as Ether Funds See $202 Million Outflow U.S. spot Bitcoin ETFs recorded $119 million in net inflows on Oct. 6, according to SoSoValue, led by BlackRock’s IBIT with $122 million. Spot Ether ETFs moved in the opposite direction, posting $202 million in net outflows, all of which came from BlackRock’s ETHA. — link

Highlight Clip: Vitalik: What Will Ethereum Look Like in Two Years? Vitalik: What Will Ethereum Look Like in Two Years? On October 6, 2026, Ethereum co-founder Vitalik Buterin said at OKX NOW in Singapore that Ethereum will support a large number of transactions in two years, with lower costs, better privacy, and deeper integration between AI and onchain applications. He suggested that both trading counterparties and application developers could be bots. Traditional applications might even cease to exist, with bots posting offers directly onchain and users' AI agents interpreting those offers and identifying suitable trading opportunities. — link

Ledger Launches Crypto Loan, Letting Users Borrow USDC or USDT Against cbBTC or wBTC Ledger launched Crypto Loan. Eligible users can post cbBTC or wBTC in Ledger Wallet and borrow USDC or USDT without selling bitcoin. Private keys and final confirmation stay on the hardware device. The feature is powered by Morpho through technical provider Yield xyz. It also adds a direct Ledger-to-Morpho connection, with no browser extension or software wallet required. It is now rolling out to eligible users. — link
